findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden; README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden'
findings.finding: Round 3's rewrite of _overridden exempts every step in the failed set from the consumption check (`s["stepId"] not in failed`). The failed set holds every step whose artefact has the subject's digest, whatever its kind. So a write tool, a delegation or a model step that consumes the failed artefact after the FAIL is accepted whenever its own artefact digest equals the failed one. unit-tests FAILs patch, then write-file consumes patch and returns the bytes it wrote: accepted (Q01). The same write returning other bytes is refused (Q01b). The round-2 model at 3ab62e34 refuses Q01 and Q03, so this is a regression. The same holds for a DELEGATE whose child delivers the same bytes (Q02) and for a MODEL copy (Q03). A tool that returns the content it stored is ordinary; a content-addressed store returns exactly this digest. This contradicts the README ('nothing but a read-only tool or a revision of the artefact consumes any of it'), H13 ('a probabilistic detector cannot override a deterministic denial') and MAS-RA-001 rule 4. Secondary: the outputs of read-only reads are followed by step ID, not by bytes, although the README says the rule follows the bytes and that none of them is delivered. A revision (Q07) or a fresh model step (Q07b) returning exactly a read's output bytes after the FAIL is gated and delivered.
findings.requiredChange: Exempt from the consumption check only read-only TOOL steps and revisions of the subject: test the step's kind and side effect instead of membership in the failed set, so a holder of another kind that consumes failed bytes after the FAIL is refused. Key the failed set by bytes throughout: every step holding the artefact of any failed step, the subject or a read. Apply that to the delivery check and to 'a revision returns other bytes' (Q07, Q07b). Add Q01 and Q02 as GATE_OVERRIDDEN vectors.

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _overridden; README 'A gate's FAIL is never overridden'
findings.finding: The failed bytes follow read-only reads 'whenever they read it'. They do not follow a write, a delegation or a model step that consumed the bytes before the FAIL, so those steps' outputs carry the failed bytes past it. write-file applies patch after schema-check passes it, unit-tests then FAILs patch, and post-ticket consumes the write's output: accepted (Q04). A model step built on patch before the FAIL is gated by schema-check alone, written and delivered: accepted (Q05). The same model step after the FAIL is refused (Q05b). A delegation handed the patch before the FAIL feeds a write after it: accepted (Q06). This is R2-1's timing dependence for the other step kinds. MAS-RA-001 rule 4 lets a deterministic FAIL 'at an intermediate' decide.
findings.requiredChange: Choose one of two options. (a) Propagate the failed set through every step that consumed failed bytes, whenever it did: its artefact is failed, and consuming it after the FAIL is refused except by a revision of the subject. (b) State three things in the README: only the artefact's bytes and read-only reads of it are failed; an earlier write, delegation or model derivation yields an artefact outside the rule; and why that agrees with H13 and MAS-RA-001 rule 4. Pin the choice with a vector (Q04 or Q05).

findings.finding: Round 3 keys the consumer reach by bytes, but the gate window still opens at the producer step: _gated needs the gate after `producer["seq"]`. A later step may regenerate bytes that an earlier step holds and a gate has already passed; a prompt-cache hit, which the vectors' profile registers, returns exactly such bytes. The earlier step's consumers are then refused. d is gated by schema-check and m later returns the same bytes. Then write-file consumes d (Q11), or d is delivered (Q11b): both are refused UNGATED_CONSUMPTION, though the bytes passed a gate before either consumer. The README's rule accepts both: 'a passing deterministic gate ... on its bytes, on any step holding them, after they are produced and before they reach a consumer'.
findings.requiredChange: Count a passing gate on any holder before the consumer. A gate's subject is always earlier than the gate, so the producer-seq lower bound can go. Add Q11 as a valid vector.

findings.finding: The two placement rules leave no room for the natural order of a hand-off after an abort. Aborting hooks must be the last steps before the HANDOFF step, and a HANDOFF-event hook must precede the HANDOFF step. So a loop whose profile registers a HANDOFF hook must record that hook before the abort that led to the hand-off. Q16 is refused TERMINAL_STATUS: an unknown non-idempotent write, the budget-stop abort, the observing 'notify' HANDOFF hook, then the HANDOFF step. Moving the notify hook before the abort is accepted (Q16b). Q21 is refused the same way: an audit hook that ERRORs (an abort, fail closed), then the HANDOFF hook, then the HANDOFF step. Round 3's R2-3 rule makes this path common: an unknown side effect now always ends in a hand-off, even after a hook abort.
findings.requiredChange: Treat HANDOFF-event hook steps directly before the HANDOFF step as part of the hand-off. Exclude them from the 'aborts are the last steps' and 'all on one event' tests: a failing HANDOFF hook changes nothing, since the loop is already handing off. Add Q16 as a valid vector.

findings.finding: A HANDOFF-event hook is accepted in a loop that never hands off. Q17: an observing HANDOFF hook in a COMPLETED loop. Q18: a HANDOFF hook that ERRORs, counts as an abort, and ends the loop ABORTED/HOOK_ABORT with no HANDOFF step. 'Not claimed' says 'a HANDOFF-event hook precedes the HANDOFF step', which reads as checked.
findings.requiredChange: Either require that a HANDOFF-event hook step be followed only by HANDOFF-event hooks and the HANDOFF step, or say in 'Not claimed' that the contract checks only that such a hook does not follow a HANDOFF step.

findings.location: README 'Revisions', 'A delegation that failed hands off', 'What a retry is'; scripts/agent_loop.py _retry_trace
findings.finding: Three statements claim more than the rules check. (1) 'A failed gate's step (its diagnosis) is consumed only by a revision of its subject, so no undeclared revision escapes the budget.' A fresh model step that consumes neither the draft nor its diagnosis is a new attempt and escapes the round budget: Q28, a further attempt delivered after the one round of revision.rounds 1 is spent. (2) The delegation rule says retrying 'would ... give it a second revision budget'. A fresh DELEGATE after the parent's own gate FAILs a COMPLETED child's artefact still gets a new child and a new budget (Q15 accepted). It is refused only if it consumes the diagnosis (Q15b). (3) 'A retry has the same kind, tool and revision target.' A GATE retry may name another gate and another subject (Q26 accepted).
findings.requiredChange: (1) Narrow the sentence to 'no step that reads the diagnosis escapes the budget'. (2) Extend the 'Disguised model retries' non-claim to undeclared revisions and re-delegations, which only the iteration and token budgets bound. (3) Either compare gateId and subjectStepId on a GATE retry, or say that gates are outside retry identity.

findings.finding: The trace is a sequence, and after a failing step only hooks may follow. So concurrent operations where one fails cannot be recorded. Q32 is refused HANDOFF_MISSING: two concurrent delegations (Harness-Zero p. 23 allows up to four), where the earlier-started child hands off and the later one completes. Q33 is refused the same way: two read-only calls launched together, where the first errors. Steps also keep start order, so the branch that completed cannot be recorded first.
findings.requiredChange: Either state in the README that v1 records a sequential loop (concurrent branches are out of scope, or the kernel serialises them), or let steps that started before the failing step ended follow it.

dispositions.evidence: _overridden adds read-only reads of the failed bytes, whenever they were made. N01 and N02 are refused GATE_OVERRIDDEN, as is N02b. Two vectors pin them ('a read-only tool reads the artefact before its gate FAILs...' and 'a model step builds on a read...'). TR_REVISE_READS_FAILED is valid, and the README says a revision may consume those reads. The same rewrite opened the holder exemption (R3-1, a regression from round 2), and other pre-FAIL consumers remain (R3-2).

_must_hand_off makes every non-OK DELEGATE hand off. N07 and N24 are refused HANDOFF_MISSING. N25 and N26 are refused UNKNOWN_REFERENCE, because their children are now invalid under R2-3. With valid children (Q12: an UNKNOWN receipt-keyed write, an abort, a hand-off; Q13: a NONE write ERROR without evidence, a hand-off), the retry is refused HANDOFF_MISSING, and so is a fresh re-delegation (Q13). Vectors cover a retried delegation after an aborted child, a FAILED child and a handed-off child. The README states that a child's bounds are the bounds.

_handoff requires HANDED_OFF after a must-hand-off step, with only hook steps between them. N09 is refused HANDOFF_MISSING and pinned by the vector 'an unknown side effect followed by a hook abort instead of the hand-off'. TR_ABORT_THEN_HANDOFF is valid. One placement side effect remains for HANDOFF-event hooks (R3-4).

GATE, HOOK and HANDOFF steps carry consumes [] and produces null in both the schema (per-kind allOf) and the model. N04 and N04b are SHAPE, and the schema rejects them. N29 is refused UNGATED_CONSUMPTION through byte-keyed holders and pinned by a vector. The README says the rule covers declared consumption. Q30 found no disagreement in 172 consumes/produces/launched mutations. Byte keying is over-strict in one case (R3-3).
In _consumers, a DELEGATE is a consumer of both producer kinds, directly or through read-only outputs. N05 and N06 are refused UNGATED_CONSUMPTION, and two vectors pin them.

_revision_bound refuses any consumer of a failed GATE step except a MODEL revision of its subject or a retry of one: Q27 is accepted. N03 and N03b are refused REVISION_BOUND, a vector pins them, and so is a DELEGATE consuming a failed gate (Q15b). The README's 'no undeclared revision escapes' wording overclaims (R3-6).

A non-OK hook step must have a null effect (HOOK_NOT_REGISTERED; Q20). It counts as an abort in _terminal, and HANDED_OFF needs an OK HANDOFF step. N11 and N12 are refused TERMINAL_STATUS, both pinned by vectors, and TR_HOOK_ERROR is valid.
ERROR_TRACE refuses an artefact on a non-OK step. N14 and P22 are refused ERROR_TRACE, and the README states the rule.

The new `launched` field appears in the schema and the model, and SHAPE agrees (Q30). A call that is not launched must FAIL with no output and no receipt; a call launched with an invalid input is refused. Both are pinned by vectors, and Q24/Q25 (not launched yet UNKNOWN) are refused INVALID_TOOL_INPUT. _unsafe_retry keys on launched. Q22 (the policy-denied receipt-keyed write, N30 with launched false) and Q23 (a denied NONE write) are accepted, and TR_DENIED_RETRY is valid.

The README says the HANDOFF step is always last and a HANDOFF-event hook is recorded before it. N13 is refused TERMINAL_STATUS and N13b is accepted. The vector 'a hook step recorded after the HANDOFF step' pins it. See R3-4 and R3-5 for what this placement now implies.

The README now limits the secrets sentence to the empty credentialRefs and leaves tool-output secrets to H11's redaction. It maps H11's side-effect classes (verified against execution.tool-skill-sandbox.md: none, reversible, compensatable, irreversible) onto READ_ONLY/WRITE. 'Not claimed' now lists approvals and the parent of a delegated trace checked alone.
